summary: Tested the mobile email login after logout and the single PIN screen (frontend at 390x844 plus desktop) and the kiosk-pin admin personal PIN block (backend). Everything the review request asked for works: logout lands on /my-awesome-rentals-bv/login?loggedout=1, then 'Inloggen met e-mail' + credentials goes straight to /admin. The PIN screen shows 'Vul je 4-cijferige pin in om verder te gaan' with no 'Andere gebruiker' button and no 'persoonlijke' text, on mobile and desktop. With a remembered device user, the admin PIN goes to /admin and the employee PIN goes to /kiosk. Without a remembered user, the admin PIN still goes to /admin through kiosk-pin. A wrong PIN shows 'Ongeldige PIN code'. Pytest: 8/8 passed. Found 1 functional bug (429 lockout) and 3 security issues in the new single-PIN design.

critical.issue: PIN collision lets an employee in as admin. personal-pin/setup does not check uniqueness against the company's employee kiosk PINs or other admins' PINs, and kiosk-pin checks admin PINs first. Reproduced: set admin PIN 4321, the same as Anita's kiosk PIN, then kiosk-pin 4321 returned admin_token with employee=null, so the kiosk employee got the admin dashboard. Reject PINs already used inside the company, in both directions (admin setup and employee PIN set).

The brute-force throttle can be bypassed by spoofing X-Forwarded-For. _client_ip takes the first XFF entry, which the client controls. 12 wrong PINs with different XFF headers all returned 401 and never 429; without the header it returned 429 after 8. kiosk-pin now issues ADMIN tokens and only needs the public company slug, so a 4-digit admin PIN can be brute-forced (10k combinations). Use the last trusted proxy hop or the real client IP, and add a per-company throttle.

minor.issue: The response includes personal_pin_hash (bcrypt hash of the 4-digit PIN), and a 4-digit hash can be cracked offline easily. Exclude personal_pin_hash and personal_pin_set_at from get_current_user / the me projection.
Returns admin_token but sets no access_token httpOnly cookie, unlike /auth/login. It relies only on the localStorage Bearer token. Inconsistent with the cookie auth model.

After the 30-min demo reset, users.anita@demo.sr is left pointing at a deleted employee_id, so PUT with email anita@demo.sr returns 409. I deleted the orphan user to continue. The demo reset should also clean up the linked users.

integration_issues.flow: Single PIN screen with device_user_email remembered (shared kiosk device)
integration_issues.issue: PinLogin.verify() calls /auth/personal-pin/login with the admin's email first. Every employee PIN therefore counts as a failed attempt in the admin's ppin throttle (key ppin:ip:email), and it is only cleared when the admin logs in successfully. After 8 employee logins the endpoint returns 429. verify() only falls through on 400/401, so on 429 it throws and shows 'Te veel mislukte pogingen...' to every user, including valid kiosk employees and the admin, for 5 min. Reproduced in the browser. Fix: kiosk-pin already recognises admin personal PINs, so call kiosk-pin first or only, or at least fall through on 429 as well; on the backend, don't count that failure.

issues: Subtitle 'Vul je 4-cijferige pin in...' is text-slate-400 on white, which is low contrast.

action_items: HIGH: Enforce company-wide PIN uniqueness between admin personal PINs and employee kiosk PINs (personal-pin/setup and employee PIN set/update).
HIGH: Fix _client_ip so a spoofed X-Forwarded-For cannot bypass the PIN throttle, and add a per-company throttle on kiosk-pin now that it issues admin tokens.

HIGH: PinLogin.verify(): stop the personal-pin/login pre-call (kiosk-pin handles admin PINs), or fall through on 429, so employee logins on an admin-remembered device don't lock everyone out after 8 logins.
Optional: set the access_token cookie in the kiosk-pin admin branch; raise the desktop subtitle contrast.
critical_code_review_comments: kiosk_pin admin loop runs bcrypt verify over up to 200 users on every PIN attempt, before the plan gate. Fine for now, but it is CPU-heavy under brute force.
MobileEmailLogin stores saved_login_password in plaintext in localStorage (pre-existing).
server.py is 18k lines; the auth/PIN routes should be split into their own module.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of requested flows (T1-T5) passed; 1 integration bug (429 lockout)

rca of the issue: 429 lockout: verify() sends every PIN to /auth/personal-pin/login(device_user_email) first. A non-matching (employee) PIN calls _pin_throttle_fail on key ppin:{ip}:{admin_email}. With PIN_MAX_ATTEMPTS=8 the key locks for 300s, and _pin_throttle_check raises 429. The frontend only swallows 400/401, so the 429 propagates to the catch and the kiosk-pin fallback is never reached. Repro: localStorage device_user_email=demo@surirent.sr, then enter the employee PIN about 8 times, then any PIN shows 'Te veel mislukte pogingen'.
